knowledge:
- key_parameters: combinedImage=Path to the composite RGB image containing all stains ;; writedir=Output directory where results (CSV and images) will be saved ;; bgCorrMethod=List specifying background correction: list(0,'') for none, list(1, sigma) for Gaussian blur, list(2, path) for user-provided illumination image, or list(3, path, pattern, n) for multidimensional correction using an image stack ;; channelSignals=List of paths to individual probe channel images (or a single composite RGB image path) ;; channelColours=List of RGB color vectors for each channel (e.g., list(R=c(255,0,0), G=c(0,255,0))) ;; sizecell=Vector of min and max area (in pixels) for nuclei segmentation (e.g., c(1000, 20000)) ;; sizeprobe=Vector of min and max area (in pixels) for probe detection (e.g., c(5, 20)) ;; maxprobes=Maximum limit for probes per nucleus; nuclei exceeding this are ignored
- alternatives: calculateMaxEntropy is preferred for reliable probe detection by maximizing inter-class entropy, whereas calculateThreshold (Otsu's method) is preferred for segmenting cell nuclei by minimizing intra-class variance.
- when_to_use: Use this package for automated, high-throughput quantification of FISH probes in cell culture images, specifically when you need to segment nuclei, detect probe signals, and calculate spatial distances between probes within each nucleus.
- pitfalls: Using composite RGB images as probe sources only works for a maximum of three probes because mixtures of red, green, and blue cannot be separated by simple color channel splitting. Ensure sufficient main memory when processing a large number of probe channels.

workflows.name: manual_threshold_and_cleanup
workflows.intent: Manually compute probe/cell masks and clean up artifacts using thresholding and particle analysis to determine optimal size parameters.
workflows.stages: 1. Read image using readImage ;; 2. Calculate threshold using calculateMaxEntropy or calculateThreshold ;; 3. Apply threshold to binarize the image ;; 4. Clean up artifacts and filter by size using analyseParticles
workflows.code:
f = system.file( "extdata", "SampleFISHgray.jpg", package="FISHalyseR")
img = readImage(f)

t = calculateMaxEntropy(img)
img[img<t] <- 0
img[img>=t] <- 1

fProbes1 = paste(TempDir,'/',"exImgMaxEntropyProbes1.jpg",sep='')
img = readImage(fProbes1)

anaImg <- analyseParticles(img, 20, 5,0)

f = system.file( "extdata", "SampleFISHgray.jpg", package="FISHalyseR")
img = readImage(f)

t = calculateThreshold(img)
img[img<t] <- 0
img[img>=t] <- 1

f = paste(TempDir,'/',"exImgOtsuCellMask.jpg", sep='')
img = readImage(f)

anaImg <- analyseParticles(img, 20000, 1000,0)

workflows.name: automated_fish_quantification
workflows.intent: Perform end-to-end automated background correction, nuclei segmentation, probe detection, and distance calculation on FISH images.
workflows.stages: 1. Define background correction method list ;; 2. Define channel signals and colors lists ;; 3. Run end-to-end pipeline using processFISH
workflows.code:
illuCorrection = system.file( "extdata", "SampleFISHillu.jpg", package="FISHalyseR")

combinedImage <- system.file( "extdata", "SampleFISH.jpg", package="FISHalyseR")
red_Og   <- system.file( "extdata", "SampleFISH_R.jpg", package="FISHalyseR")
green_Gn <- system.file( "extdata", "SampleFISH_G.jpg", package="FISHalyseR")

# directory where all the files will be saved
writedir = paste(TempDir,sep='')

bgCorrMethod = list(0,'')

channelColours = list(R=c(255,0,0),G=c(0,255,0))
channelSignals = list(red_Og,green_Gn)
sizecell = c(1000,20000)
sizeprobe= c(5,20)

processFISH(combinedImage,writedir,bgCorrMethod,channelSignals,
            channelColours,sizecell,sizeprobe)
